# Welcome to my website!

Hello! My name is Zuhair Khan. I’m a graduate student and staff member in the Department of Population and Quantitative Health Sciences at CWRU School of Medicine, where I’m pursuing a master’s in Biomedical and Health Informatics and working as an Enrollment Specialist.

Before coming to CWRU, I completed my MPH at the University of Miami and earned my BS in Molecular and Cellular Biology from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. I also worked as a community health worker, which helped shape my interest in the intersection of health data, equity, and systems-level change.

My academic and professional interests lie in clinical and translational sciences, with a focus on quantitative methods, healthcare services, and management. I’m especially interested in improving the quality and affordability of healthcare delivery in the U.S. through evidence-based policy and operational improvements. In the future, I hope to pursue a PhD in health policy or a related field like health management or operations research to contribute meaningfully to this space.

I’ve had the opportunity to work in a range of healthcare settings, which deepened my understanding of the structural challenges within our system—and the levers we can use to create more equitable and effective care.

I’m originally from New Orleans and grew up in Chicago after Hurricane Katrina. I’m the proud child of two Indian Muslim immigrants and part of a big, loving family. I’m also lucky to have great friends, two amazing older siblings, a wonderful brother-in-law, and a chubby orange cat. In my free time, I enjoy learning, volunteering, reading, making music, laughing, dancing, and exploring new food and cultures.

Please feel free to check out my background and CV to learn more!
